newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks post second straight record close.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks post second straight record close.

text.p: Toronto's key stock index posted its second straight record close on Friday, rallying in expectation of improved quarterly profits in the upcoming reporting season.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index jumped 33.48 points to 6626.40, also breaking its former all-time intraday high.
"The market is anticipating better second-quarter earnings," said Montreal-based portfolio manager Ron Meisels.
Some earnings already have begun to trickle in.
Investors were also bargain hunting in Toronto's battered gold sector, Meisels said, spurring modest gains in one of its most heavily weighted groups.
Canada's largest equities market reached a new intraday record of 6633 points, capping a week of gains. The 300 index rose 64 points this week from Monday's open of 6562.
The transportation sector led nine of Toronto's 14 sub-indexes higher, followed by golds, industrial products, media and forestry products.
The weaker side included oils and base metals.
Turnover was healthy at 95 million shares worth C$1.5 billion ($1.1 billion).
Advancing issues outnumbered declines 564 to 391, while 300 traded flat.

Among individual issues, Geac Computer Corp. Ltd. soared 9.50 to 47.50 in brisk dealings. It posted fourth-quarter earnings of C$0.70 per share on Thursday, up 131 percent from last year's C$0.31 a share.
Barrick Gold Corp., the world's third largest gold miner, gained 0.60 to 30.55, continuing to rebound from weakness earlier this week when gold bullion prices fell to 12-year lows.
Elan Energy Inc. dropped 1.25 to a 52-week low of 8 on almost 3.4 million shares after an analyst reported a gloomy outlook for the oil company's production, financial and stock performance.

Shares in Air Canada rose 0.50 to 11.30, a 52-week high, after news that it and other members of the recently launched Star Alliance held a two-day meeting in Germany to try to negotiate a global cargo alliance.
